units: Architecture specification defines software architecture intended to implement Adaptive Inheritance.
Architectural objective: E* -> Phi_R(e_t) -> Delta W -> W_{t+1}.
Five responsibilities: constraint failure detection, residual attribution, authority redistribution, representation expansion gating, empirical validation.
AIC requires invalidated mechanisms to lose inherited influence; immediate replacement is not required.
Layer order is PTVS, MRAT, Adaptive Inheritance, REE, RAHU.
PTVS detects local violations and measures empirical friction without modifying mechanisms.
LBR is violations divided by total generated paths.
PTVS interface specifies TrajectoryBatch and EnvironmentConstraints inputs and a PTVSReport output.
MRAT determines the lowest structural level responsible for failure and is intended to prevent unnecessary modification.
MRAT attribution vector a=(a_N,a_S,a_M,a_R,a_G), components sum to 1.
MRAT interface specifies residual/PTVS/current-mechanism inputs and AttributionVector output.
Layer 3 modifies mechanism authority based on empirical validity.
ARR = invalid post-authority divided by invalid pre-authority.
Authority half-life is first time invalid authority is at most half its initial value.
Inheritance interface specifies FailureAttribution and MechanismWeights inputs and UpdatedWeightDistribution output.
REE expansion is admissible only when lower-order adaptation is insufficient.
REE gate combines residual saturation with positive expected adaptive gain over representation cost.
Expansion should be rejected when expected future gain does not exceed representation cost.
RAHU is intended to externally measure whether the architecture maintains empirical coupling without hidden-state inspection.
Source asserts module dependency path ptvs -> mrat -> inheritance, with inheritance feeding ree and rahu.
Architecture should operate using externally observable behavior and not require chain-of-thought access.
Minimal intervention objective minimizes adaptation cost subject to restoring empirical coupling.
Capability and corrigibility are asserted to be separate axes.
Successful implementation must detect contradiction, attribute residual, redistribute authority, modify structure parsimoniously, and reduce invalid mechanism influence.
Architecture is considered validated when E* -> Phi_R -> Delta W -> W_{t+1} is externally observable.
Document describes itself as a paper-to-code contract without prematurely committing to implementation details.
No estimator or identification procedure is specified for producing empirically warranted attribution probabilities across N/S/M/R/G.
The architecture does not define how mechanism authority weights acquire causal interpretation from observable behavior.
The architecture does not specify estimators for residual compressibility, expected future gain, or representation cost.
No validation protocol is supplied establishing that ADI or ACS are calibrated measures of the claimed constructs.
The phrase 'externally observable' does not itself specify an experimental design sufficient for causal identification of the full chain.
